newsitem.title: USA: Chubb Q4 falls below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Chubb Q4 falls below expectations.

text.p: Chubb Corp's fourth quarter operating earnings fell below Wall Street's expectations, with results hurt by higher catastrophe losses.
Chubb reported record fourth quarter operating earnings of $0.95 a share compared to analysts' First Call estimate of $0.99.
Catastrophe losses nearly quadrupled in the fourth quarter to $33.9 million from $8.6 million in the 1995 fourth quarter.
The impact of the catastrophe losses on the fourth quarter earnings was $0.12 a share compared to $0.03 a share a year ago. Chubb shares closed Thursday at 55, up 3/8.

"Producing a solid underwriting profit and record operating income are impressive accomplishments, especially given the higher catastrophe losses we experienced in 1996," Chubb chief executive Dean O'Hare said.
For the year, catastrophe losses were $141.7 million compared to $63.7 million in 1995.
However, Chubb said its 1996 results were helped by strong growth in its personal lines and overseas businesses.
Net premiums written in the personal lines business were $1.04 billion in 1996, up from $866.8 million in 1995.
In the commercial lines business, however, net premiums written were $3.53 billion in 1996 compared to $3.07 billion in 1995.
"Personal lines completed an excellent year, with strong growth and a combined ratio of 91.7 percent," O'Hare said.
"Commercial lines produced growth and achieved a combined ratio of 99.7 percent, no small feat in the current environment," he said.

"Overseas, we continued to grow rapidly as the result of both increasing levels of indigenous business in international markets and the development of more global accounts for which we provide coverage in multiple international locations," he said.
Overall, net premiums written rose 10.9 percent to $4.8 billion in 1996 compared to $4.3 billion in 1995.
For the year, about one-third of the premium growth was due to changes in the quota share reinsurance agreements with the Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc.
These changes resulted in Chubb retaining a greater portion of its business written directly while assuming less reinsurance from Royal & Sun Alliance.
Changes in certain casualty reinsurance programs also contributed to the premium growth in 1996, Chubb said.
The complete unwinding of the exchange of reinsurance between Chubb and Royal and Sun Alliance became effective January 1, 1997, Chubb said.
Life and health insurance income after taxes were $12.9 million for the fourth quarter compared with $6.2 million a year ago.
For the year, life and health insurance income was $40.3 million compared with $28.0 million in 1995.
Real estate income after taxes was $3.2 million in the fourth quarter compared to $2.5 million a year ago.
For the full year, real estate income after taxes was $13.2 million in 1996 compared with $6.0 million in 1995.
Chubb said it continued to repurchase shares of its common stock during the fourth quarter. A total of 1.7 million shares were repurchased in the open market in 1996.
